- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history with 0.00 values suggests low market confidence; model should be conservative, underpredicting by 1–3% for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 0.33 or higher, model should be more aggressive but not exceed 5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
